facts.raw_span: A man in his 70s with no history of chronic or allergic rhinosinusitis
presented to the emergency department with a headache for 2 weeks
vision loss in the right eye for 2 days
Three weeks prior, he had rhinorrhea and was diagnosed with COVID-19
Right eye visual acuity was limited to hand-motion detection
severe pain on ocular motion
Opacification of all sinuses on the right with diffuse inflammation
Bony erosion of the medial orbital apex bone, with extension of inflammation into the apex
Serum IgG4: 277 mg/dL (normal, <123 mg/dL)
Sinus Cultures: Positive for Streptococcus constellatus
Dense infiltrate of IgG-containing plasma cells, with most being IgG4 positive
Right-sided headache 1 week later and right vision loss 2 days prior to presentation
A man in his 70s with no history of chronic or allergic rhinosinusitis
presented to the emergency department with a headache for 2 weeks
vision loss in the right eye for 2 days
Three weeks prior, he had rhinorrhea and was diagnosed with COVID-19
Right eye visual acuity was limited to hand-motion detection
severe pain on ocular motion
Opacification of all sinuses on the right with diffuse inflammation
Bony erosion of the medial orbital apex bone, with extension of inflammation into the apex
Serum IgG4: 277 mg/dL (normal, <123 mg/dL)
Sinus Cultures: Positive for Streptococcus constellatus
Dense infiltrate of IgG-containing plasma cells, with most being IgG4 positive
Right-sided headache 1 week later and right vision loss 2 days prior to presentation

concepts.why: Elevated serum IgG4 levels and dense infiltrate of IgG-containing plasma cells with most being IgG4 positive support this diagnosis.
Opacification of all sinuses on the right with diffuse inflammation and positive sinus cultures for Streptococcus constellatus suggest chronic rhinosinusitis.
Bony erosion of the medial orbital apex bone with extension of inflammation into the apex and vision loss in the right eye support this diagnosis.
Bony erosion of the medial orbital apex bone with extension of inflammation into the apex and vision loss in the right eye are consistent with Tolosa-Hunt syndrome.
Opacification of all sinuses on the right with diffuse inflammation and positive sinus cultures for Streptococcus constellatus could be seen in granulomatosis with polyangiitis.
Opacification of all sinuses on the right with diffuse inflammation and dense infiltrate of IgG-containing plasma cells could be seen in sarcoidosis.
Opacification of all sinuses on the right with diffuse inflammation and positive sinus cultures for Streptococcus constellatus could be seen in eosinophilic granuloma with polyangiitis.
Opacification of all sinuses on the right with diffuse inflammation and positive sinus cultures for Streptococcus constellatus could be seen in invasive fungal sinusitis.

Opacification of all sinuses on the right with diffuse inflammation and bony erosion of the medial orbital apex bone with extension of inflammation into the apex are consistent with rhino-orbital mucormycosis.
Opacification of all sinuses on the right with diffuse inflammation and positive sinus cultures for Streptococcus constellatus could be seen in aspergillosis.

rationales.F03: Vision loss in one eye is a key feature of C03
rationales.F07: Opacification of all sinuses on the right with diffuse inflammation is consistent with C02 and invasive fungal sinusitis
rationales.F08: Bony erosion of the medial orbital apex bone is a strong indicator of C03
rationales.F09: Elevated Serum IgG4 levels are highly suggestive of C01
rationales.F10: Positive sinus cultures for Streptococcus constellatus could be seen in C02 or invasive fungal sinusitis
rationales.F11: Dense infiltrate of IgG-containing plasma cells with most being IgG4 positive is highly suggestive of C01

frontier_selector.rationale: High serum IgG4 levels and dense infiltrate of IgG4-positive plasma cells support IgG4-related disease, which can cause orbital apex syndrome, explaining the patient's vision loss and headache.
